method: Read every supplied field and reasoned through each key, distractor, rationale, objective and difficulty. Targeted primary-source checks are recorded separately; a reference alone was not treated as validation.
limitations: Not external clinician or psychometric validation
Source verification is targeted; general educational and communication principles were reviewed for internal and clinical coherence.

sourceChecks.method: Primary Canadian Paediatric Society page retrieved through search and opened
sourceChecks.finding: Newborn jaundice and feeding concerns need clinical evaluation; reviewed the principle, not treatment thresholds or bilirubin calculations.

sourceChecks.method: Primary PHAC postpartum chapter retrieved through search and opened
sourceChecks.finding: Postpartum warning patterns include infection findings and sudden heavy bleeding with dizziness; no exact numeric treatment threshold introduced.

items.assessment: The item honestly tests foundation knowledge: past agreement and relationship status do not establish current voluntary consent. The explanation separates consent from contraception and absence of objection.
Private postpartum pain assessment is correct, but annual delay, emotional-only attribution and partner substitution are conspicuous errors.
issues: Private postpartum pain assessment is correct, but annual delay, emotional-only attribution and partner substitution are conspicuous errors.
proposedChanges: Compare assessment of healing/symptoms with lubricant advice, a routine postpartum appointment and pelvic-floor referral. Give timing and symptoms so assessment determines which support is appropriate.

items.assessment: Reviewing pregnancy prevention is appropriate, but three nonkeys restate the same unsupported infertility assumption while the key is the only comprehensive clinical action.
issues: Reviewing pregnancy prevention is appropriate, but three nonkeys restate the same unsupported infertility assumption while the key is the only comprehensive clinical action.
proposedChanges: Compare continuing current contraception pending review, switching to symptom/cycle tracking, requesting menopause assessment and changing to a barrier method. Give relevant age/history if needed; do not invent a universal stopping interval.

items.assessment: An evolving asymmetric colour-changing lesion merits assessment despite no pain, but year-long delay, moisturizer and usual tanning make it too easy.
issues: An evolving asymmetric colour-changing lesion merits assessment despite no pain, but year-long delay, moisturizer and usual tanning make it too easy.
proposedChanges: Compare prompt assessment with serial photographs, planned routine skin review and self-monitoring for bleeding. Make the timing and documented evolution distinguish clinical review; avoid an invented urgency threshold.

items.assessment: Medication review, oral prevention and hydration assessment are appropriate, but stopping all prescribed medicines independently is a caricature sole nonkey.
issues: Medication review, oral prevention and hydration assessment are appropriate, but stopping all prescribed medicines independently is a caricature sole nonkey.
proposedChanges: Replace with a realistic attempted remedy such as frequent sugary lozenges and explain caries risk. Consider an actual dry-mouth case with relevant medication timing and oral findings.

items.assessment: Adapting protection/timing preserves useful gardening, but indefinite cessation and cloudy-day-only medication are extreme distractors.
issues: Adapting protection/timing preserves useful gardening, but indefinite cessation and cloudy-day-only medication are extreme distractors.
proposedChanges: Compare protective clothing/timing, higher sunscreen SPF alone, taking the medicine at night and relying on shade. Explain which plan addresses exposure without independently altering treatment.

items.assessment: Food access assessment is correct, but flavour-only and trusting advertising are implausible professional alternatives.
issues: Food access assessment is correct, but flavour-only and trusting advertising are implausible professional alternatives.
proposedChanges: Compare buying a supplement, a feasible food plan, referral for nutrition review and a food-support resource. Add ability to eat and absence of a prescribed supplement need to distinguish the immediate plan.

items.assessment: Accessible activity planning is appropriate, but all nonkeys repeat walking/standing as exclusive goals; overlaps149.
issues: Accessible activity planning is appropriate, but all nonkeys repeat walking/standing as exclusive goals; overlaps149.
proposedChanges: Use concrete available wheelchair-accessible exercise options and actual upper-limb endurance or shoulder limitations. Compare goals that differ in feasibility and required rehabilitation assessment rather than generic inclusivity.

items.assessment: Respectful correction is correct, but insulting intelligence and ending the class are cartoon professional responses.
issues: Respectful correction is correct, but insulting intelligence and ending the class are cartoon professional responses.
proposedChanges: Compare clarifying the evidence to the group, speaking privately after class, inviting participant sources and distributing a later resource. Give an immediately consequential claim so timely public clarification is best.

items.assessment: Nonattender input and community partnership fit the reach problem, but only-satisfaction signals the nonkey.
issues: Nonattender input and community partnership fit the reach problem, but only-satisfaction signals the nonkey.
proposedChanges: Remove only and phrase the competing evaluation directly, e.g surveying current attendees about convenience. Explain why it does not adequately represent people the service is failing to reach.

items.assessment: Worsening jaundice with unusual sleepiness is a genuine warning pattern, but the key contains an explicit reassuring alternative and sunlight/feet thresholds are conspicuous foils.
issues: Worsening jaundice with unusual sleepiness is a genuine warning pattern, but the key contains an explicit reassuring alternative and sunlight/feet thresholds are conspicuous foils.
proposedChanges: Shorten the key to prompt clinical assessment. Compare feeding-support visit, repeat weight check and bilirubin/clinical assessment pathways, ensuring hard-to-wake status calls for urgent assessment rather than routine scheduling. Add a direct CPS newborn jaundice source.

items.assessment: Fever, pelvic pain and foul discharge support prompt assessment; activity for drainage and leftover antibiotics are implausible nurse advice.
issues: Fever, pelvic pain and foul discharge support prompt assessment; activity for drainage and leftover antibiotics are implausible nurse advice.
proposedChanges: Compare prompt assessment with hygiene review, temperature recheck after an antipyretic and a scheduled postpartum review. Add actual postpartum day and fever if useful, and explain why the combined infection cues override routine care.

items.assessment: The client is explicitly cleared to mobilize after uncomplicated birth. Gentle planned movement is appropriate; delaying until bleeding stops, substituting ankle movement and relying on compression each reflect plausible overcautious prevention choices with specific limits.
Sudden heavy bleeding and faintness warrant emergency help, but overnight recording and routine activity are exaggerated delays.
issues: Sudden heavy bleeding and faintness warrant emergency help, but overnight recording and routine activity are exaggerated delays.
proposedChanges: Compare emergency activation with calling the routine postpartum line, arranging family transport and resting with oral fluids while monitoring. Explain why possible circulatory compromise favours emergency response; keep options similar length.

items.assessment: Feeding, breathing and alertness warning signs matter, but a major feeding change waiting a month is a cartoon sole nonkey.
issues: Feeding, breathing and alertness warning signs matter, but a major feeding change waiting a month is a cartoon sole nonkey.
proposedChanges: Use actual caregiver observations, including a benign transient feeding/sleep variation versus persistent poor feeding, difficult waking or respiratory distress. Clarify emergency escalation for significant breathing difficulty rather than an undifferentiated contact route.

items.assessment: Whole-child context is correct, but all-care-from-fever and never-deteriorates are extreme absolutes against a comprehensive key.
issues: Whole-child context is correct, but all-care-from-fever and never-deteriorates are extreme absolutes against a comprehensive key.
proposedChanges: Use two or more short concrete child observations or plausible assessment priorities. Specify age if fever urgency is tested and compare behaviour, hydration, breathing and measured temperature without an all-encompassing uniquely long key.

items.assessment: Honest sensations and coping support are appropriate; equipment brand is irrelevant and caregiver-all-answers weak.
issues: Honest sensations and coping support are appropriate; equipment brand is irrelevant and caregiver-all-answers weak.
proposedChanges: Compare an honest brief description with demonstration of equipment, distraction, caregiver explanation and reassurance as appropriate. Replace the brand foil and keep the response developmentally direct.

items.assessment: Coordinated current guidance is correct, but memory-alone and exclusion-from-every-session advertise poor care.
issues: Coordinated current guidance is correct, but memory-alone and exclusion-from-every-session advertise poor care.
proposedChanges: Name one concrete practice difference and compare shared demonstration/teach-back, giving a current leaflet, asking parents to relay guidance and scheduling a separate caregiver session. Explain why consistent practical understanding is needed.

items.assessment: Simple responsive play is valid, but price-predicts-benefit and only-specialized-toys are broad marketing caricatures; label does not match direct recall.
issues: Simple responsive play is valid, but price-predicts-benefit and only-specialized-toys are broad marketing caricatures; label does not match direct recall.
proposedChanges: Compare concrete play experiences such as caregiver turn-taking with simple objects, prerecorded electronic prompts and independent activity-centre play. Either add infant cues for an applied decision or label foundation.

items.assessment: Reassessment and adaptation fit a new work schedule, but interpreting change as failed learning is an implausible sole nonkey.
issues: Reassessment and adaptation fit a new work schedule, but interpreting change as failed learning is an implausible sole nonkey.
proposedChanges: Replace with a plausible plan action, such as retaining the previous meal timing until the next routine review or compensating with one larger meal. Add shift/meal access cues so adaptation options are clinically and practically grounded.
